questionText:
Match List-I with List-II

List-I (Judge/Leader)
(A) Justice A.N. Ray
(B) Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha
(C) Justice J.C. Shah
(D) George Fernandes

List-II (Appointment/Judgement/movement)
(I) A retired Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India, who inquired into several aspects of allegations of abuse of authority, excesses and malpractices committed and action taken in the wake of the emergency
(II) A leader who called for a nationwide strike by all employees of the railways in 1974
(III) Chief Justice of India in 1973
(IV) A Judge of Allahabad High Court who passed a judgement declaring Indira Gandhi’s election to the Lok Sabha invalid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence (Chapter 6: The Crisis of Democratic Order): (A) Justice A.N. Ray was appointed Chief Justice of India in April 1973 superseding three senior judges (Match III). (B) Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha of the Allahabad High Court delivered the landmark verdict on 12 June 1975 setting aside Indira Gandhi's election to the Lok Sabha from Rae Bareli (Match IV). (C) Justice J.C. Shah headed the Shah Commission of Inquiry in 1977 into emergency excesses (Match I). (D) George Fernandes led the National Coordination Committee for Railwaymen's Struggle in May 1974 (Match II). Matching: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.

questionText: Which among the following is not a cultural consequence of globalisation?

options.text: Deregulation of industries
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: The fear of threat to cultures
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: The powerful hegemonic influence of western culture
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Cultural exchange
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics (Chapter 9: Globalisation, pp. 136-141): Globalisation impacts are divided into three clear categories: (1) Political (erosion of state capacity), (2) Economic (trade deregulation, FDI flows, WTO rules, deregulation of industries), and (3) Cultural (threat to indigenous cultures, western cultural homogenisation, burger/blue jeans culture, cultural exchange, and heterogenisation). Therefore, 'deregulation of industries' is strictly an economic policy dimension.
Hence, option (A) is correct.

questionText:
Arrange the following events in chronological order.
 
(A) Antarctic Treaty
(B) Rio Summit
(C) Brundtland Report
(D) Kyoto Protocol
 
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Timeline of international environmental milestones:
1. (A) Antarctic Treaty: Signed in Washington on 1 December 1959.
2. (C) Brundtland Report ('Our Common Future'): Published by the World Commission on Environment and Development in 1987.
3. (B) Rio Summit (Earth Summit / UNCED): Held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil in June 1992.
4. (D) Kyoto Protocol: Adopted in Kyoto, Japan on 11 December 1997.
Correct sequence: (A), (C), (B), (D).
Hence, option (B) is correct.
